query: From March 631 to April 631, Farrukhzad Khosrau V was the king of an empire that succeeded which empire?

pipeline_result.response: From March 631 to April 631, Farrukhzad Khosrau V was the king of an empire that succeeded the Sasanian Empire. The Sasanian Empire had been ruled by the House of Sasan and its successor the Parthians until the latter's dissolution in 1806.
retrieved_context: Farrukhzad Khosrow V: Farrukhzad Khosrau V was briefly king of the Sasanian Empire from March 631 to April 631.  He was the son of Khosrau II.

Sasanian Empire: The Sasanian Empire ( or ), also known as the Sassanian, Sasanid, Sassanid or Neo-Persian Empire, known to its inhabitants as Ērānshahr in Middle Persian, was the last period of the Persian Empire (Iran) before the rise of Islam, named after the House of Sasan who ruled from 224 to 651 AD.  The Sasanian Empire, which succeeded the Parthian Empire, was recognised as one of the leading world powers alongside its neighbouring arch-rival the Roman-Byzantine Empire, for a period of more than 400 years.

Austrian Empire: The Austrian Empire (Austrian German: "Kaiserthum Oesterreich" , modern spelling "Kaisertum Österreich ") was a Central European multinational great power from 1804 to 1867 created by proclamation out of the realms of the Habsburgs.  It was the third most populous empire after Russia and France, as well as the largest and strongest country in the German Confederation.  Geographically, it was the second largest empire in Europe after the Russian Empire (621,538 square kilometres [239,977 sq mi]).  Proclaimed in response to the First French Empire, it overlapped with the Holy Roman Empire until the latter's dissolution in 1806.  The "Ausgleich" of 1867 elevated Hungary's status.  It became a separate entity from the Empire entirely, joining with it in the dual monarchy of Austria-Hungary.
